blocks.html: The crime of forgery is here patent: by the change of name and the substitution of the person, the said du Tilh having asserted that he was called, and was, Martin Guerre: for although it is lawful for everyone to change his name at his pleasure a2, inasmuch as names are imposed only to recognise persons and to distinguish them one from another b2: this nevertheless is understood with good faith, and without intention to defraud or injure another c2. As when Pope Sergius, the second of that name, who was called in Italian Bocca di porco, that is to say Pig's Mouth, had himself named Sergius: whence since then the Pontiffs of Rome have drawn the custom of leaving, at their creation, their proper name, to take another — after the example also (as they say) of Jesus Christ, who gave the name of Peter to Simon Bar-Jona when he chose him for his disciple. d2 Provided therefore that the intention be not evil, one may change not only one's name, but also one's surname and arms e2, and call oneself of another country: as when St Paul, in the Acts of the Apostles, called himself a citizen of Rome, although he was none f2. And Jesus Christ, speaking of St John, said that he was Elijah g, whom the Lord God had promised by the Prophet h: not, says St Augustine, that Jesus understood St John to be the very person of Elijah, but by imitation of virtue i. Otherwise, whoever changes his name must be punished and repressed by the penalty of forgery x, and such a one (said the Jurisconsult Ulpian in some place) that he may be an example to others l [unclear: the print reads & telle, (diſoit en quelque lieu le Iuriſconſulte Vlpien qu'il en ſoit) autres aux exemple, with the parenthesis closed too late and autres aux inverted; translated by the evident sense].

notes.citation: Code 9.25 (De mutatione nominis), l. unica (C. 9.25.1, Diocletian and Maximian) — the print's D. for C.
notes.original: l. vn D. de mura no.
notes.gloss: The sole law of the title: as the imposition of a name is a private matter, so its change is without danger to the innocent, provided it is done without fraud (sine aliqua fraude). Cited at annot-012 {b} under its right book.

notes.citation: Code 7.14 (De ingenuis manumissis), l. Ad recognoscendos (C. 7.14.10, Diocletian and Maximian); Institutes 2.17 (Quibus modis testamenta infirmantur), § 5, at the words sed quia (sed quia sane commodius erat singulas causas singulis appellationibus distingui)
notes.original: l. ad recognoſcendos. C. de ingen. & man. P. ſed quia. qui modis teſt. infir.
notes.gloss: Names are imposed to recognise individuals; as at annot-012 {a}, where the Institutes passage cited is instead Inst. 2.20.29 on error in a legatee's name.

notes.citation: The same sole law (C. 9.25.1), and Coras's Annotation XII above (cross-reference to annot-012)
notes.original: l. vnique al leguee. Et ci deſſus en l'anotarion,⟨alt:notation,⟩ xij.

notes.citation: Pietro Crinito (Pierre Crinit), De honesta disciplina, book 3 (or 4), chapter 10 as printed — the passage on Pope Sergius not located in the 1543 edition (OCR); book and chapter unverified
notes.original: Pierre Crinit. ru iij.⟨alt:iiij.⟩ de honeſta diſcipli. c. x.
notes.gloss: For Pope Sergius Os porci and the papal custom of taking a new name; the print's ru is au.

notes.citation: Decretals of Gregory IX, title De excessibus praelatorum et subditorum, c. Dilecta (X 5.31.14, Honorius III), and Panormitanus (Panorme) on it
notes.original: c. dilecta. là où Panorme de exceſ. pralaror.
notes.gloss: For the lawful change of surname and arms.
Paul at Philippi declares himself a Roman.
"This is Elias, which was for to come."
"Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet."

notes.citation: Decretum of Gratian, Part II, C. 22 q. 2, c. Quaeritur (Augustine; cf. C. 22 q. 2 c. 22)
notes.gloss: Augustine on figurative speech that is not a lie — John called Elijah by likeness of spirit, not identity of person. Cited again at annot-081 {g} for Jacob.

notes.citation: Digest 48.10 (De lege Cornelia de falsis), l. Falsi (D. 48.10.13 pr., Papinian)
notes.gloss: The assertion of a false name or cognomen is punished with the penalty of falsum — the text Coras's whole annotation rests on; cited also at annot-012 {c}. The margin keys this note x, as the body marker is read; the alphabet expects k.

notes.citation: Digest, title abbreviated de reb. cor. — not resolved; the fragment beginning Quamvis not identified
notes.original: l. quamuis. D. de reb. cor.
notes.gloss: Cited again, with the same abbreviation, at annot-081 {a} for exemplary punishment; the Ulpian saying Coras paraphrases, that the penalty should be an example to others, has not been located under this title.

notes.citation: unidentified (sigla incomplete: no canon of D. 10, and no incipit in Friedberg's index, begins Sive adulterium)
notes.gloss: Perhaps a canon of the Decretum, Part I, Distinctio 10; its place in the argument is not evident.
